# TITLE LINUX SECURITY HANDBOOK # SUBTITLE 5. SUID, SGID, STICKY BIT, AND ACLs # BADGES PAGE 5 OF 20 # SECTION_HEADINGS - SUID EXECUTABLES - SPECIAL PERMISSION TYPES - SGID FILES AND DIRECTORIES - STICKY BIT - ACCESS CONTROL LISTS (ACLs) - GETFACL AND SETFACL - SEARCHING FOR SUID AND SGID BINARIES - FIND SUID/SGID FILES - ACL COMMANDS EXAMPLES - UNEXPECTED PRIVILEGE PATHS - AUDITING SPECIAL PERMISSIONS - AUDIT CHECKLIST # BODY_PARAGRAPHS **SUID EXECUTABLES** When a file has the SUID bit set, it runs with the permissions of the file owner (usually root). Risk: Can be abused to gain elevated privileges. Check SUID files regularly. **SGID FILES AND DIRECTORIES** SGID on files: Runs with the group owner's privileges. SGID on directories: New files inherit the directory's group ownership. Helps in controlled group collaboration. **STICKY BIT** On directories, only the file owner, directory owner, or root can delete or rename files. Common on /tmp to prevent users from deleting each other's files. **ACCESS CONTROL LISTS (ACLs)** Provide fine-grained permissions beyond the traditional user/group/other model. Useful for granting access to specific users without changing ownership. **GETFACL AND SETFACL** getfacl : View ACLs on files and directories setfacl : Modify ACLs for fine-grained access ACLs override standard permissions. **SEARCHING FOR SUID AND SGID BINARIES** Regularly search for SUID/SGID files to detect unexpected privilege escalation paths. New or unknown files can be a security risk. **UNEXPECTED PRIVILEGE PATHS** Attackers exploit misconfigured SUID/SGID files or writable paths to escalate privileges. Always verify owner, permissions, and purpose. **AUDITING SPECIAL PERMISSIONS** Maintain an inventory of all special permission files. Review regularly and document approved exceptions. Remove unnecessary permissions immediately. # IMPORTANT_FILES *(No specific file paths listed as storing data, only commands referencing paths like /path/to/file, /bin, /sbin, etc.)* # TABLES | **SPECIAL PERMISSION TYPES** | | | :--- | :--- | | **S** | **SUID (4xxx)**
Run as file owner | | **S** | **SGID (2xxx)**
Run as group owner | | **T** | **STICKY (1xxx)**
Restricted deletion | | **A** | **ACLs**
Extended permissions | | **AUDIT CHECKLIST** | | | :--- | :--- | | ✅ | Review all SUID, SGID, and Sticky files | | ✅ | Verify file purpose and ownership | | ✅ | Ensure directories with SGID are required | | ✅ | Check ACLs for unnecessary access | | ✅ | Document approved exceptions | | ✅ | Remove or fix unnecessary entries | # COMMANDS **Find all SUID files:** `find / -type f \( -perm -4000 \) -exec ls -l {} \; 2>/dev/null` **Find all SGID files:** `find / -type f \( -perm -2000 \) -exec ls -l {} \; 2>/dev/null` **Find SUID and SGID in common paths:** `find /bin /sbin /usr/bin /usr/sbin /usr/local/bin -type f \( -perm -4000 -o -perm -2000 \) -ls 2>/dev/null` **View ACLs:** `getfacl /path/to/file` **Add ACL entry:** `setfacl -m u:user:rw /path/to/file` **Remove ACL entry:** `setfacl -x u:user /path/to/file` **Remove all ACLs:** `setfacl -b /path/to/file` # TIPS_NOTES_WARNINGS *(No explicit "Tip", "Note", or "Warning" boxes present; content is integrated into body paragraphs and checklists)* # PRACTICAL_EXERCISES *(No specific numbered practical exercise steps provided)* # FOOTER_TEXT VERIQTA YouTube @veriqta GitHub @veriqta LinkedIn @veriqta X @veriqta Instagram @veriqta Telegram @veriqta VERIQTA # PAGE_NUMBER 5 OF 20
